item.title: Democrats Win in Landslide, US Stock Futures Rebound
item.description:
A Democratic sweep of Congress rippled across global markets, with stocks fluctuating while the dollar fell and Treasuries gained on bets the outcome will put the brakes on President Donald Trump’s agenda.
Futures for the S&P 500 rose 0.2% while those for the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.3%. Both fell earlier before buyers stepped in. The dollar weakened against major peers, while 10-year Treasury yields fell three basis points to 4.93%. Europe’s Stoxx 600 climbed 0.6% and a gauge for Asian equities was little changed.
The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game. Hosted by Anna Edwards, Guy Johnson and Tom Mackenzie. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Mortgage Rates Retreat for Third Week While Holding Above 7%
item.description: US mortgage rates fell for a third straight week, though a decline in purchase activity showed borrowing costs remain prohibitively high for many prospective buyers.

item.title: San Francisco’s BART Gets Lifeline as Voters Approve New Tax
item.description: The struggling public-transit system in the San Francisco Bay Area received a financial lifeline Tuesday, with voters passing a proposed sales tax to fund the region’s trains, buses and ferries.

item.title: US Bonds Rise on Democrat Win With Focus Moving to Debt Plan
item.description: US Treasuries rallied as the Democrats swept to power in Congress, pointing to a political environment that may limit the Trump administration’s tax and spending plans.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Nov. 4
item.description: Oil edged lower, extending a two-day decline as traders weighed signs of de-escalation from the US while results from key midterms elections rolled in.
